newsitem.title: BELARUS: Lukashenko votes, defends Belarus referendum.
newsitem.headline: Lukashenko votes, defends Belarus referendum.

text.p: President Alexander Lukashenko voted on Sunday in a controversial referendum on increasing his powers and said he had no doubt that Russia and other foreign states would regard the result as valid.
Referring to his long-running conflict with parliament and the constitutional court, he told reporters: "After the referendum all these fights will vanish."
He attacked parliament for scuppering a compromise deal brokered by Russia on Friday and said he would act according to the result of the voting.
The main question out of seven put to the voters is approval of a new constitution extending his term in office and widening his powers.
"I do not doubt that foreign states and Russia will recognise the referendum as legitimate," he said after casting his ballot at a sports college in Minsk.
By 10 a.m. (0800 GMT) 29.3 percent of the electorate had voted, including those who cast their ballots ahead of time, electoral official Lidiya Yermoshina told Belarussian television.
Around 1,000 anti-Lukashenko demonstrators continued to protest outside parliament but otherwise the capital was calm.
